pl-l2d35c5-d1e108.summary: Explains that one withdraws from God by sin not by distance of place, since he is wholly present everywhere and is not a place; his temple is the clean soul in which he dwells. One is far from God by departing from his likeness, the further the more unlike. Augustine: things like God by participation can become unlike, but Likeness itself, the Son, cannot be unlike the Father in any part; nothing makes man so unlike God as sin. Sin as privation of good in the soul is also privation of the body's good, depriving it of the immortality and impassibility it had before sin.
claims: The Son cannot be unlike the Father.
Sin deprived the body of immortality.

pl-l2d35c5.summary: Explains that one withdraws from God by sin not by local distance, since God is wholly present everywhere and is not a place; the clean soul is called his temple because he dwells in it. One is far from God by departing from his likeness, the further the more unlike. Augustine: things similar to God by participation can become dissimilar, but Likeness itself, the Son, cannot; nothing makes man so unlike God as sin. Sin as privation of good in the soul also deprives the body, as it removed the immortality and impassibility it had before sin.
claims: Distance from God by sin is unlikeness, not place.
God is wholly present everywhere and is not in a place.
The clean soul is God's temple.
Creatures like God by participation can become unlike; the Son as Likeness cannot.
Nothing makes man so unlike God as sin.
Sin also deprived the body of immortality and impassibility.
